Commentary.Commentary: We are back for the run chase! The umpires are back out in the middle and so are the Indian players, who form a huddle and take their places on the field. Surprising to see that George Linde has been sent in to open the innings for South Africa alongside Aiden Markram. Arshdeep Singh is ready to start proceedinngs with the new ball. Let's play...
... The Run Chase ...

A daunting task awaits South Africa - 241 is what South Africa need to get their campaign in the sub-continent underway and it will be a test of their batting depth now. India have a plethora of pacers and spinners to choose from and they will be confident of defending this total. However, the pitch looks flat and there will be opportunities for the batters to go big, and it should be an exciting chase. Stay tuned.

An evening to forget for the Proteas in the field - A side boasting of such depth in the pace attack has simply been dismantled tonight. Aiden Markram gave one-over spells to all his 6 pacers in the Powerplay and none of them could do anything to restrict the opposition. Spin didn't make much difference either but when they slowed it up or changed their lengths, there was some purchase on offer. Anrich Nortje was taken to the cleaners, and so were most of the bowlers but the likes of Marco Jansen and Lungi Ngidi did comeback in their spells later on.

India flex their batting might - That is a swashbuckling first 20 overs with the bat from India and they have put a daunting total on the board. It was carnage through and through from the Indian batters but Ishan Kishan up top was the most impressive. He was retired out after a quickfire half-century and so was Abhishek Sharma, who scored 24 runs. Tilak Varma came back into the main team and it was like he never left as he made 45 off just 19 balls. Everyone in the Indian middle order contributed and Hardik Pandya's feisty cameo of 30 runs off just 10 balls was the icing on the cake.
Oh, Corbin Bosch has gotten away with it. Even the crowd shows their frustration! Too short and down leg, Harshit Rana leaves it alone. India end with a massive 240/6 on the board.

Commentary.Commentary: DRINKS BREAK! Ishan Kishan is being retired out now. Well, that was entertaining. The Proteas bowlers will be happy to see Kishan walking back, not sure about the crowd, though. Anyway, South Africa will now look to regroup and reassess their plans. Meanwhile, India will look to continue the carnage and make full use of that deep batting lineup. Also, Tilak Varma comes in to replace Ishan Kishan now.

SIX! BOOM! That will be FIFTY FOR KISHAN. This is a bit slower and fuller from Kwena Maphaka, on middle and off. Ishan Kishan clears his front foot and slogs it across the line over deep mid-wicket fence for six more runs. He lifts his willow and soaks up all the applause from the supporting fans watching his strokeplay.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 5.4: Kwena Maphaka to Ishan Kishan, Six!

Commentary.Commentary: On a hard length, on middle and off. Ishan Kishan hangs a bit back and once again tries to slap it through cover, but fails to get the connection.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 5.3: Kwena Maphaka to Ishan Kishan, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Back of a length, outside off, Ishan Kishan looks to cut at it but gets beaten on the outside edge.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 5.2: Kwena Maphaka to Ishan Kishan, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Full, on off, Abhishek Sharma flicks it to square leg and gets a single.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 5.1: Kwena Maphaka to Abhishek Sharma, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: This is surreal hitting from Ishan Kishan. Is this a warm-up game or an exhibition match? Now, the sixth pacer comes into the attack in the form of Kwena Maphaka.

SIX! Nothing is working for South Africa right now! This is a well-directed bouncer, on middle, around the helmet of the batter. Ishan Kishan looks to pull, but the ball comes big at him. Kishan removes his sight on the delivery, but fails to lower his willow. The ball hits the top edge of the bat and luckily the ball loops over short fine leg for four runs.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 4.6: Anrich Nortje to Ishan Kishan, Six!

Commentary.Commentary: FOUR! Ishan Kishan moves into the 40's now! Fuller, on middle, Ishan Kishan uses his bottom hand and punches it upishly over the mid on region for four runs.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 4.5: Anrich Nortje to Ishan Kishan, Four!

Commentary.Commentary: SIX! The crowd is loving it as Ishan Kishan is just not stopping! Back of a length, on leg and middle. Ishan Kishan lifts his front leg up and this time he flicks it with a bit power to sail it over deep fine leg for another biggie.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 4.4: Anrich Nortje to Ishan Kishan, Six!

Commentary.Commentary: SIX! Oh, this is outstanding batting from Kishan! Nortje pitches it hard, on the length around the hips of the batter. Ishan Kishan just rolls his wrists and flicks it with the perfect timing to lob the delivery over deep fine leg for six more runs.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 4.3: Anrich Nortje to Ishan Kishan, Six!

Commentary.Commentary: On a length, angling across the off stump. Abhishek Sharma looks to heave it across the line, but gets the inside edge and hits on the pad. The ball rolls away to cover and the batter gets a quick single.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 4.2: Anrich Nortje to Abhishek Sharma, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: SIX! Up, up and over! This is on a good length, on middle and off. Abhishek Sharma makes room on the leg side, skips down the track and opens the face of the bat to slash it over the sweeper cover fence for half a dozen. 50 comes up for India.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 4.1: Anrich Nortje to Abhishek Sharma, Six!

Commentary.Commentary: The fifth pace bowler is now on for South Africa in the first 5 overs. Anrich Nortje comes on to bowl, replacing Kagiso Rabada.
14 runs off Bosch's first over. Gets the stumps into play, around off and touch short. Kishan tries to fend it away but misses and it rolls to the keeper.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 3.6: Corbin Bosch to Ishan Kishan, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Corbin Bosch finally bowls one to the field! A slower bumper on leg, Abhishek Sharma pulls but mistimes it to the left of Kwena Maphaka at deep square leg, who palms it back and keeps it down to a single.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 3.5: Corbin Bosch to Abhishek Sharma, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: FOUR! Streaky but it all counts. Length is slightly short, width on offer. Abhishek Sharma throws the kitchen sink at it and edges it past Anrich Nortje at short third man for a boundary.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 3.4: Corbin Bosch to Abhishek Sharma, Four!

Commentary.Commentary: FOUR! India beginning to motor on now. A bit too full on this occasion, outside off, Abhishek Sharma crunches on the up, over extra cover and it races to the fence.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 3.3: Corbin Bosch to Abhishek Sharma, Four!

Commentary.Commentary: FOUR! One-bounce four! Hard length delivery, little bit of width. Abhishek Sharma says thank you as he hammers it over mid off and finds his first boundary.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 3.2: Corbin Bosch to Abhishek Sharma, Four!

Commentary.Commentary: Bosch bangs it short, outside off, Kishan slashes it straight to deep point for a single.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 3.1: Corbin Bosch to Ishan Kishan, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: Pitches it up, around off, Sharma goes for timing rather than power and hits it straight to mid off.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.6: Kagiso Rabada to Abhishek Sharma, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: That should have been put away! A rare occasion where Abhishek Sharma missed out. A low gentle full toss on the pads. Sharma fails to put his bat on it.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.5: Kagiso Rabada to Abhishek Sharma, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Leg bye! Touch short and on middle and leg, a bit into the surface. Kishan is rushed as he tries to help it away.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.4: Kagiso Rabada to Ishan Kishan, Leg bye.

Commentary.Commentary: SIX! This is clean as a whistle from Kishan! Rabada overcorrects and pushes it full and on middle and leg, Ishan Kishan stands tall and punishes it over mid-wicket for a six. Third already for Ishan.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.3: Kagiso Rabada to Ishan Kishan, Six!

Commentary.Commentary: Gives width outside off but KG bowls the off-cutter across the batter. Abhishek Sharma slaps it to deep point for one.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.2: Kagiso Rabada to Abhishek Sharma, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: Wide! Length ball from over the wicket, well down leg. Sharma fails to connect it.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.2: Kagiso Rabada to Abhishek Sharma, Wide!

Commentary.Commentary: Rabada attacks the stumps straight up with a length delivery. Abhishek Sharma punches it to cover.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.1: Kagiso Rabada to Abhishek Sharma, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: FOUR! Belted away! Slightly loose from Jansen as he tries the slower delivery but overpitches it in the slot. Kishan lofts it over mid off and it rolls to the fence.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.6: Marco Jansen to Ishan Kishan, Four!

Commentary.Commentary: Can Marco Jansen close out the over well? Just 3 off it so far but this is the extra ball he has to bowl because of the wide.
WIDE! Gets it to swing into the batter but bowls it down the leg side. Ishan looks to clip it away but msises.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.6: Marco Jansen to Ishan Kishan, Wide!

Commentary.Commentary: What an excellent grab from Ryan Rickelton behind the stumps. Shaping away, fuller and down the leg side, Kishan swings across and misses. Ryan Rickelton dives to his right and pouches with his right hand.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.5: Marco Jansen to Ishan Kishan, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Abhishek Sharma is off and running! Length delivery, outside off, Abhishek Sharma uses the room to carve it to deep point for a single.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.4: Marco Jansen to Abhishek Sharma, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: Extra bounce on this one, too! Short of a good length on the hips. Sharma tries to work the angle away but fails and wears it on the pads.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.3: Marco Jansen to Abhishek Sharma, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Into the surface, hard length and gets good bounce off the surface, around off. Abhishek Sharma makes room and flashes hard but miscues off the inner half of the bat, back to Jansen.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.2: Marco Jansen to Abhishek Sharma, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Jansen pushes it through, fuller and around the fifth stump line. Kishan pats it past backward point for a single.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.1: Marco Jansen to Ishan Kishan, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: Marco Jansen is ready to operate from the other end.
A gentle full toss, around off, dips onto the batter, Kishan eases it to mid on and keeps the strike. 14 runs off the first over.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.6: Lungi Ngidi to Ishan Kishan, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: SIX! Helped away effortlessly! Lungi Ngidi errs in line, little bit of swing on offer but too straight on the pads. Ishan Kishan gets his wrists into play as he flicks it over square leg for a six.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.5: Lungi Ngidi to Ishan Kishan, Six!

Commentary.Commentary: Tries the slower fuller delivery and bowls it around off, Ishan Kishan presses forward and knocks it to cover.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.4: Lungi Ngidi to Ishan Kishan, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Lungi Ngidi corrects his length and drags it a bit short, around off and seaming away. Ishan Kishan is squared up as he leans across to push it away but misses.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.3: Lungi Ngidi to Ishan Kishan, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: SIX! DISMISSED! First of many expected today! Pitched up, in the slot on middle. The ball doesn't do much and Ishan Kishan launches it over long on for a massive six.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.2: Lungi Ngidi to Ishan Kishan, Six!

Commentary.Commentary: WIDE. Lungi Ngidi gets away here! Shorter, straighter and on leg. Ishan Kishan looks to pull it away but misses.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.2: Lungi Ngidi to Ishan Kishan, Wide!

Commentary.Commentary: Bowls on a good length, around off, shaping back in. Ishan Kishan, without much foot movement, punches it to cover.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.1: Lungi Ngidi to Ishan Kishan, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: All in readiness for the game to begin. The umpires are out in the middle and the South African players can be seen in a huddle before striding onto the field of play. It will be the duo of Abhishek Sharma and Ishan Kishan to open the innings for India. Ryan Rickelton is actually donning the keeping gloves, not Quinton de Kock. Lungi Ngidi has the new ball in hand and is raring to go. Let's play...

Pitch Report - Abhinav Mukund starts off saying that 430 runs were scored in the match between India A and USA on this pitch. Nick Knight joins the analysis and says that there's not much grass on the ball, and reckons that the ball will carry on this track. Also says the team winning the toss can do whatever they want, as it's a warm-up match and the teams have all the liberty to try out different new things.

The captain of South Africa - Aiden Markram expresses satisfaction with the decision to bowl first, noting that the toss alignment offered South Africa a valuable opportunity to readjust to Indian conditions. Acknowledging the significant shift from the playing environment in South Africa, he remained optimistic that the team’s recent experience in India would accelerate their acclimatisation process. Markram emphasises that the squad is clear on its starting combinations and individual roles, shifting the primary focus towards rebuilding collective rhythm and executing their established game plan as they settle into the series.

India's captain - Suryakumar Yadav describes the venue as a paradise for batters, citing a recent high-scoring match between India A and USA. Affirms that Ishan Kishan and Abhishek Sharma will be opening the innings for them in this game. He mentions that the pitch to be used tonight is similar to the one in the previous match and expects it to have pace and carry. Yadav believes dew won't be a major factor and predicts a run-feast tonight, given the nature of the pitch. Yadav calls the pitch a belter and suggests that the teams should enjoy the warm-up game before the real competition begins.

South Africa - Aiden Markram (C), Quinton de Kock (WK), Ryan Rickelton, David Miller, Dewald Brevis, George Linde, Jason Smith, Marco Jansen, Tristan Stubbs, Corbin Bosch, Anrich Nortje, Kagiso Rabada, Keshav Maharaj, Kwena Maphaka and Lungi Ngidi.

India - Abhishek Sharma, Ishan Kishan, Sanju Samson (WK), Suryakumar Yadav (C), Tilak Varma, Hardik Pandya, Rinku Singh, Shivam Dube, Washington Sundar, Axar Patel, Harshit Rana, Arshdeep Singh, Jasprit Bumrah, Kuldeep Yadav and Varun Chakaravarthy.
TOSS - Up goes the coin, and it lands in favour of Suryakumar Yadav. India have opted to BAT first!

Final chance to sharpen the tools - The Proteas’ success may ultimately hinge on their adaptability to local conditions and on the hope to go one step further than their previous runner-up finish. As both giants fine-tune their strategies in Navi Mumbai, expect some fireworks under the lights in the warm-up game. Toss coming up next.

The Proteas look to go one better - South Africa heads into the tournament with a reshaped squad following injuries to Tony de Zorzi and Donovan Ferreira. While David Miller works back to full fitness, the Proteas rely on the 'red-hot' Quinton de Kock and captain Aiden Markram. Late additions Ryan Rickelton and Tristan Stubbs add spark, but the team's tournament hopes may rest on how surprise pick Jason Smith and spinners Keshav Maharaj and George Linde adapt to the turning tracks of India and Sri Lanka.

Unanswered questions - India’s selection dilemmas highlight their strength. Ishan Kishan is challenging Sanju Samson for the gloves, while Axar Patel is expected to edge out Kuldeep Yadav to provide extra batting cushion. With a pace attack led by Jasprit Bumrah and the mystery spin of Varun Chakaravarthy, the Men in Blue look well-equipped to defend their crown on home soil. This game might end up being an audition for those couple of spots still up for grabs in the Playing XI come the opeinng game of the mega event.

Rematch of the 2024 Final - The T20 World Cup returns to the subcontinent as defending champions India and runners-up South Africa face off in a marquee warm-up match at Navi Mumbai’s DY Patil Stadium. India enter the tournament as the heavy favorite, boasting immense depth and recent momentum from a 4-1 series win over New Zealand. Despite injury concerns for Washington Sundar and Tilak Varma, the squad remains lethal with Abhishek Sharma and Suryakumar Yadav in peak form, supported by the clinical finishing of Rinku Singh and Hardik Pandya.
... MATCH DAY ...

Sharpening steel before the battle begins - The stage is set for a high-voltage clash as two of the most dangerous outfits in T20 cricket go up against each other, not for points, but for polish. With the ICC T20 World Cup 2026 just around the corner, India and South Africa meet one last time to tighten the loose ends and sharpen the rough edges in a warm-up clash at the DY Patil Sports Academy, Navi Mumbai. Sure, it’s officially just a practice game with nothing tangible on the line. But scratch the surface and there’s plenty at stake. Combinations to lock in, roles to clarify, nerves to settle, and statements to be made. Routes mapped ahead - Let’s quickly take a look at where these two sides stand in the main draw. South Africa find themselves in Group D, alongside strong contenders Afghanistan and New Zealand, with Canada and UAE completing the group. India, meanwhile, are slotted into Group A, placed alongside Pakistan, and also featuring challengers in the form of USA, Namibia, and the Netherlands. Rampaging India - In their recent assignment, India found a lot of positives, especially in the batting department. Abhishek Sharma has been operating in top gear, setting the tone up front and giving the side the kind of starts every T20 team craves. Ishan Kishan, fresh off a statement century, has made it clear that he is very much here to stay. Add to that Suryakumar Yadav easing back into form, along with a middle order packed with power and timing, and India’s batting unit is beginning to look well-oiled at just the right moment. The bowlers, more often than not, found themselves on the receiving end, but that is part of the territory in a high-scoring series. The likes of Arshdeep Singh and Jasprit Bumrah, along with Harshit Rana, will be keen to tighten things up, find their rhythm back alongside a frugal spin trio. The Proteas charge with fire in veins - With a top order featuring Quinton de Kock, Aiden Markram and Ryan Rickelton, there is very little to separate them when it comes to firepower. The Proteas showed just how destructive they can be when they chased down a historic 222 in only 17.3 overs, with de Kock smashing a century and Rickelton breezing his way to 77 against West Indies. The one area they will be keen to shore up is the middle order. Youngsters Dewald Brevis and Tristan Stubbs, along with the experienced David Miller, will want to turn promising starts into decisive contributions. On the bowling front, spinners Keshav Maharaj and George Linde will look to make the most of the spin-friendly conditions, backed by a genuinely lethal pace attack spearheaded by Kagiso Rabada and Marco Jansen. It’s all about momentum - Both teams walk in riding a serious wave of confidence. South Africa were sharp and ruthless at home, brushing aside West Indies 2-1 with barely a crack in their armour. India, on the other hand, sent out a statement of their own, taking down New Zealand 4-1 and ticking most of the boxes along the way. So when these two sides come up against each other, it is less about labels and more about rhythm. Two in-form teams built on a reputation of a ruthlessly aggressive style of cricket in the shortest format get one final chance to carry that momentum cleanly into the World Cup. Should be an engaging one.
